subject.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)

question: Should omitted-detached Unix cleanup fall back to direct-PID signaling when process-group leadership cannot be verified, after the current base conflicts are resolved?
rationale: The code path fixes a real gateway SIGTERM failure, but it changes shared process cleanup defaults and may leave descendants for unverifiable omitted callers; that compatibility and availability tradeoff needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup After Rebase
options.body: Resolve the dirty merge state, rerun exact-head validation, and land this leader-check approach if direct-PID fallback is accepted as the safer default for unverifiable omitted callers.

options.title: Require More Explicit Caller State
options.body: Ask for additional caller forwarding or tests before merge if maintainers want fewer omitted cleanup paths to depend on runtime process-group detection.

options.title: Pause The PR
options.body: Keep this unmerged or close it if maintainers decide any omitted-caller descendant cleanup risk is worse than the current gateway process-group SIGTERM risk.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup After Rebase
recommendation.body: Resolve the dirty merge state, rerun exact-head validation, and land this leader-check approach if direct-PID fallback is accepted as the safer default for unverifiable omitted callers.
